title: The Pandora Campaign
description: The starting campaign for new Pandora MMO groups.

crossroads_tavern.name: The Crossroads Tavern
crossroads_tavern.description: A weathered inn where every road out of town seems to meet. The fire never quite warms the back corner.

sensory_connections.whispering_wood: A rutted dirt road runs west out of the yard, straight for a stretch before curving out of sight toward a dark, unbroken tree line — the Whispering Wood, farther off than it looks from the tavern steps.
sensory_connections.stonearch_bridge: East, past the last few rooftops, the road narrows and climbs toward a low stone rise — Stonearch Bridge is up and over that rise, out of sight until you're most of the way there.

hearth_mantle.name: the hearth mantle
hearth_mantle.description: Carved dates and initials from a hundred travelers crowd the old wood, half worn smooth by hands running over them for luck.

regulars_board.name: the corkboard by the door
regulars_board.description: Taped-up notices, faded flyers, a couple of crude wanted posters. One scrap of paper has no name and no signature, just three words in shaky charcoal: IT COUNTS DOORS.

grimsbys_ledger.name: the heavy ledger behind the bar
grimsbys_ledger.description: Grimsby keeps it within arm's reach at all times and has never once let anyone else turn a page.

market_row.name: Market Row
market_row.description: A crooked street of stalls and shopfronts. A locksmith here has stopped taking new keys to cut.

marens_scale.name: Old Maren's brass scale
marens_scale.description: An ornate weighing scale on the counter. Maren swears by its accuracy, but it never quite balances evenly, even with identical weights on both sides.

shuttered_stall.name: a boarded-up stall
shuttered_stall.description: Nailed shut from the outside, which is the strange part — nobody in Market Row admits to knowing who used to run it.

locksmiths_keys.name: rows of hanging keys in the locksmith's window
locksmiths_keys.description: Dozens of unlabeled keys, none cut to any lock still in use in town, as far as anyone will say. Someone still dusts them.

marens_strongbox.name: Old Maren's locked strongbox
marens_strongbox.description: An old strongbox Maren's lost the combination to. A riddle is carved into its lid, worn but still legible: "I have cities, but no houses; forests, but no trees; rivers, but no water. What am I?"

the_colosseum.name: The Colosseum
the_colosseum.description: A weathered ring of stone stands apart from the market's noise, its sand still dark in patches from bouts nobody talks about after. A challenger's bell hangs by the gate, worn smooth from use.

whispering_wood.name: The Whispering Wood
whispering_wood.description: An old forest where the leaves move without wind. Locals say the trees remember things.

resource_nodes.name: a stand of old, sturdy timber
a rotted log slumped under the low bushes

listening_tree.name: an ancient, wide-boled tree
listening_tree.description: Its bark seems to almost resolve into faces at the edge of your vision — never quite there when you look straight at it.

carved_waystone.name: a weathered waystone
carved_waystone.description: A trailside marker carved with a script no one in the Crossroads can read, in strokes too regular to be natural weathering.

whispering_wood_deep_glade.name: The Deep Glade
whispering_wood_deep_glade.description: The canopy closes overhead here, thick enough that even the leaves' restless movement comes through muffled, like something heard through a wall.

resource_nodes.name: a stand of deadfall timber, dry and untouched

glade_hollow_ring.name: a perfect ring of mushrooms
glade_hollow_ring.description: Too even to be natural, too old to be anyone's doing. Nothing else grows inside it.

whispering_wood_mossy_creek.name: The Mossy Creek
whispering_wood_mossy_creek.description: A slow, quiet creek threading between the roots. The water runs clear enough to see the bottom, and still no one fishes it after dark.

resource_nodes.name: a soft mudbank along the creek's edge

creek_stones.name: a line of flat stepping stones
creek_stones.description: Worn smooth and evenly spaced, as if placed rather than found — though no one living remembers placing them.

whispering_wood_bramble_thicket.name: The Bramble Thicket
whispering_wood_bramble_thicket.description: Brambles grown into a wall taller than a person, with exactly one gap wide enough to push through. Something kept it that way.

thicket_gap.name: the single gap through the brambles
thicket_gap.description: Just wide enough for one person at a time, thorns pulled back and tied off with old, sun-bleached cord.

whispering_wood_elder_glen.name: The Elder Glen
whispering_wood_elder_glen.description: The oldest trees in the Wood stand here in a loose, deliberate circle, bark carved smooth by centuries of wind. Locals say the trees remember things — here, it feels like they're the ones doing the watching.

resource_nodes.name: a rare, pale patch of Silverleaf Herbs

the_watching_circle.name: the ring of ancient, wind-smoothed trees
the_watching_circle.description: Stand in the center and the leaves go still, all at once, all around you — the only place in the whole Wood where they ever stop moving.

elder_carved_riddle.name: words worn into the widest tree's bark
elder_carved_riddle.description: Carved so long ago the bark's grown almost smooth over it, but still legible: "I have many rings but no fingers, many arms but no hands, and I tell your age without ever asking. What am I?"

hollow_stump_shrine.name: The Hollow Stump Shrine
hollow_stump_shrine.description: A shrine built into the base of a tree wider than a house, long since dead. Offerings left here are never touched by animals.

resource_nodes.name: Moonpetal flowers growing at the shrine's base

offering_line.name: a row of small offerings
offering_line.description: Trinkets, coins, and dried flowers laid out at the shrine's base with an unnerving, exact symmetry no one seems to have arranged on purpose.

stumps_rings.name: the stump's growth rings
stumps_rings.description: Visible where the outer bark has fallen away. One ring, deep in, is far darker than all the others — as if that entire year burned instead of grew.

greymoor_downs.name: The Greymoor Downs
greymoor_downs.description: Rolling grey hills under a sky that seems one shade too dim, even at noon.

resource_nodes.name: a scatter of loose stones at the base of the standing stones

standing_stones.name: a loose ring of standing stones
standing_stones.description: Weathered megaliths, all leaning in the same direction, like something long ago pushed the whole hill sideways at once.

old_bandit_camp.name: a cold, abandoned campsite
old_bandit_camp.description: Ash gone stiff and grey, and a boot print frozen in old mud, pointed toward the road rather than away from it.

greymoor_downs_windswept_ridge.name: The Windswept Ridge
greymoor_downs_windswept_ridge.description: A high spine of rock along the Downs, wind loud enough here to cover most other sound. Good for seeing a long way. Good for not being heard, too.

ridge_cairn_markers.name: a line of small stacked-stone markers
ridge_cairn_markers.description: Spaced too evenly to be idle piling, all pointing the same direction along the ridge — toward the cairn further north.

greymoor_downs_lonely_cairn.name: The Lonely Cairn
greymoor_downs_lonely_cairn.description: A single burial cairn, well kept for something no one admits to visiting. Whoever tends it doesn't want to be found doing it.

the_cairn_itself.name: the cairn's carefully fitted stones
the_cairn_itself.description: No name carved anywhere on it, but the topmost stone is always clean — swept clear, again and again, of whatever the wind piles onto it.

greymoor_downs_below_the_cairn.name: Below the Cairn
greymoor_downs_below_the_cairn.description: A narrow shaft under the cairn's foundation stone, dug by hand and refilled by hand, over and over, by whoever keeps coming back. Nothing down here looks like it's resting.

the_refilled_shaft.name: the shaft's carefully refilled walls
the_refilled_shaft.description: Packed and re-packed so many times the dirt's gone smooth. Somebody keeps digging this back open, and somebody keeps closing it again.

the_wedged_marker.name: a weather-stained marker, wedged sideways into the shaft wall
the_wedged_marker.description: Not local stone — carried here, then left. Scratched into its face, in a hand that matches nothing else down here, is a story about someone called Pandora, who was given a box she never asked for and told only that she must never open it — and who spent the rest of her life proving that being told 'never' isn't the same as being told 'why.' The marker doesn't say what was inside. It doesn't say she opened it, either. It just says she kept the box, and kept asking, until the day she didn't need an answer anymore. Nothing else here explains why it's buried under a cairn on the far side of a world it clearly wasn't carved in.

greymoor_downs_broken_watchtower.name: The Broken Watchtower
greymoor_downs_broken_watchtower.description: A collapsed watchtower, half its height still standing. From the top of what's left, the bridge crossing is fully visible — every safe way across, and every way that isn't.

resource_nodes.name: loose stones scattered through the tower's collapsed base

watchtower_vantage.name: the tower's remaining upper landing
watchtower_vantage.description: Rotted through in two places, but still holds — and still gives the clearest view of the bridge crossing for miles.

stonearch_bridge.name: Stonearch Bridge
stonearch_bridge.description: An ancient stone bridge spanning a gorge no one remembers naming. Half the carvings on its rail have worn past reading.

resource_nodes.name: the stream running through the gorge below
the muddy bank beneath the bridge, pocked with tiny burrows

worn_carvings.name: the bridge's worn rail carvings
worn_carvings.description: Half worn past reading, the other half still legible enough to make out a procession of small figures, all facing the same direction, toward the far bank.

gorge_below.name: the gorge beneath the bridge
gorge_below.description: Looking down, the sound that rises up doesn't quite match falling water — closer to something breathing, slow and even.

stonearch_bridge_far_end.name: The Far End of the Span
stonearch_bridge_far_end.description: Where the bridge finally lets out past the gorge, onto a narrow shelf of rock before the land opens up again. Quieter here — the gorge's sound doesn't carry this far.

far_end_marker.name: a single carved marker stone
far_end_marker.description: Newer than the bridge itself by centuries, but already weathering to match — someone wanted it to look like it had always been here.

the_weeping_well.name: The Weeping Well
the_weeping_well.description: A well that hasn't run dry in living memory, though no one draws from it anymore. It is always slightly warmer than the air around it.

lockables.name: a sealed stone door low in the well's wall

wells_rim.name: the well's warm stone rim
wells_rim.description: Warm to the touch no matter the season, with a faint hum that seems to rise and fall with no particular rhythm.

door_carvings.name: carvings ringing the sealed stone door
door_carvings.description: Spirals cut deep into the stone, none of them repeating exactly, all of them circling inward toward the door itself.

well_water.name: the water sitting still at the bottom of the well
well_water.description: Clear all the way down, with nothing floating in it and nothing growing on its walls -- water that's sat this long anywhere else would be thick with algae by now.

tavern_cellar.name: The Tavern Cellar
tavern_cellar.description: A low stone cellar beneath the Crossroads Tavern, close with the smell of old wood and older wine.

resource_nodes.name: a patch of pale fungus growing in the damp corner

marked_barrel.name: a barrel with a chalk symbol
marked_barrel.description: Every other barrel down here is unmarked. This one has a circle-and-line symbol chalked on its lid, redrawn recently enough that the dust hasn't settled on it.

cellar_shelf.name: a shelf of dusty bottles
cellar_shelf.description: Vintages going back further than the tavern's own sign out front. A few labels have worn away entirely.

tavern_upstairs.name: The Tavern's Upper Rooms
tavern_upstairs.description: A narrow hallway of guest rooms above the common room, quiet but for the creak of old floorboards.

room_seven_door.name: the door at the end of the hall
room_seven_door.description: Every other guest room door stands slightly ajar or plainly numbered. This one is shut, unmarked, and noticeably colder to stand near than the hallway around it.

guestbook.name: a guestbook on the landing table
guestbook.description: Names going back years, most in different hands. A handful of entries near the middle of the book are scratched out so hard the pen tore the page.

the_arcane_nook.name: The Arcane Nook
the_arcane_nook.description: A gap between two shopfronts on Market Row, barely wide enough to walk through, that most people swear wasn't there yesterday. It always is, if you're looking for it.

vanes_shelves.name: shelves of curiosities behind the counter
vanes_shelves.description: Nothing on them is labeled, and no two items seem to be from the same era, region, or maker — yet somehow none of it looks out of place next to the rest.

the_uneven_floor.name: the shop's oddly uneven floor
the_uneven_floor.description: The floorboards slope gently toward the back of the nook, just enough to notice, never enough to explain.

sunken_root_caverns.name: The Sunken Root Caverns
sunken_root_caverns.description: Caves threaded with the pale, massive roots of something above. The air smells faintly of rain that never falls down here.

resource_nodes.name: a vein of Sulfur Dust in the cavern wall
a shelf of pale fungus clinging low to the massive root

massive_root.name: the cavern's massive pale root
massive_root.description: Wide enough to walk along like a bridge. Pressing a hand to it, you'd almost swear it shifts, slow as a held breath.

damp_alcove.name: a damp stone alcove
damp_alcove.description: Old claw marks score the walls here, layered over each other by what must have been years of the same animal returning to the same spot — or several animals never learning better.

goblin_warrens.name: The Goblin Warrens
goblin_warrens.description: A cramped, chattering network of tunnels. Someone, or something, has been organizing the goblins here far better than goblins usually organize themselves.

resource_nodes.name: a seam of Iron Ore the goblins have been chipping at

chalk_markings.name: chalk markings on the tunnel walls
chalk_markings.description: Goblin scrawl, but organized — arrows, tallies, what might be a crude map — in a hand far steadier than goblins are known for.

makeshift_totem.name: a crude bone totem
makeshift_totem.description: Lashed together from bits of scavenged bone and wire, and kept in far better repair than anything else the goblins have bothered to maintain.

glimmerdeep_grotto.name: Glimmerdeep Grotto
glimmerdeep_grotto.description: Vast caverns lit by crystal formations that pulse very slowly, like something breathing. Some of the crystals have gone a wrong color.

wrong_crystal.name: a crystal pulsing off-rhythm
wrong_crystal.description: Every other formation in the grotto breathes in the same slow unison. This one pulses to its own beat, faintly, and a shade of color none of the others share.

grotto_pool.name: a still, black pool
grotto_pool.description: The water is perfectly still, and reflects the ceiling above — except for one patch, near the center, that seems to reflect something else entirely.

sunken_root_caverns_deep_tunnels.name: The Deep Tunnels
sunken_root_caverns_deep_tunnels.description: Passages that keep going long after they should have ended. Somewhere ahead, rubble chokes one of them almost shut — almost.

tunnel_rubble_choke.name: a passage nearly sealed by old rubble
tunnel_rubble_choke.description: Almost fully collapsed, but not quite — cleared enough times, by something or someone, to still be worth clearing again. Air moves through it from somewhere else entirely.

sunken_root_caverns_forgotten_cistern.name: The Forgotten Cistern
sunken_root_caverns_forgotten_cistern.description: A dry, ancient cistern, long since cut off from whatever it used to hold. Someone stashed something down here and never came back for it.

lockables.name: a sealed cache half-buried in dry silt

cistern_dry_channels.name: the cistern's dry drainage channels
cistern_dry_channels.description: Cut with real precision, leading nowhere any water could reach anymore. Someone built this to hold something other than water.

sunken_root_caverns_precise_channel.name: The Precise Channel
sunken_root_caverns_precise_channel.description: A single channel, cut with the same exact precision as the cistern's drainage, leading further down than anything else in these caverns goes. The stonework here isn't goblin work, and it isn't natural either.

channel_matching_stonework.name: stonework that matches something else, somewhere else
channel_matching_stonework.description: The same exact cut, the same exact angle, as stories describe far below the earth in places no one from up here has ever actually seen.

goblin_warrens_inner_den.name: The Inner Den
goblin_warrens_inner_den.description: Deeper into the warrens than most goblins bother going. Whatever discipline holds the outer tunnels together frays out completely back here.

resource_nodes.name: a scatter of unrefined ore the goblins never bothered collecting

den_bone_pile.name: a disorganized pile of gnawed bones
den_bone_pile.description: The one thing back here that ISN'T organized — everything else in these warrens is unnervingly tidy by comparison.

glimmerdeep_grotto_glimmering_pool.name: The Glimmering Pool
glimmerdeep_grotto_glimmering_pool.description: A second, smaller pool tucked behind the grotto's main chamber, lit from below by something buried in the silt at its bottom.

lockables.name: a corroded coffer resting on the pool's floor

pool_buried_light.name: whatever's glowing at the bottom of the pool
pool_buried_light.description: Too deep to make out clearly, and it never stops glowing, no matter how long you watch it.

the_hush_below.name: The Hush Below
the_hush_below.description: A cavern so silent that your own footsteps seem to arrive a half-second late. Nothing living seems to want to be here, including, increasingly, you.

silent_footprints.name: footprints pressed into old dust
silent_footprints.description: Fresh enough that the dust hasn't resettled, in a size and stride that match no one currently down here.

old_iron_door.name: an old iron door, ajar
old_iron_door.description: Rusted through in places, standing open just enough to see there's nothing but more dark on the other side. It wasn't open a moment ago.

the_first_city.name: The First City
the_first_city.description: An impossibly old city, buried and forgotten, built by hands unfamiliar with any craft practiced above. Its central spire is still, somehow, faintly warm.

warm_spire.name: the city's central spire
warm_spire.description: Warm under your palm despite the age and the dark, with the faintest rise and fall to it, like something enormous breathing very slowly.

unfamiliar_glyphs.name: glyphs carved into every visible surface
unfamiliar_glyphs.description: A script that matches nothing above ground, repeated so often it starts to feel less like writing and more like counting.

the_first_city_outer_ward.name: The Outer Ward
the_first_city_outer_ward.description: A ring of buried structures further out from the spire, walls still standing at odd, deliberate angles no living architect would choose. Whatever lived here built for reasons, not just shelter.

ward_angled_walls.name: walls set at impossible, deliberate angles
ward_angled_walls.description: Every angle is different, and every angle is exact — nothing here is broken or worn, only built strangely on purpose.

the_first_city_spire_reaches.name: The Spire Reaches
the_first_city_spire_reaches.description: The upper reaches of the buried city, close enough to the central spire to feel its warmth without touching it. The glyphs here are denser, and some of them move, slightly, when you're not looking directly at them.

resource_nodes.name: an unnaturally pure vein of ore laced through the stone

reaches_shifting_glyphs.name: a dense cluster of restless glyphs
reaches_shifting_glyphs.description: Watched directly, they hold perfectly still. Watched from the corner of your eye, more than one of them is moving.

the_first_city_sunken_archive.name: The Sunken Archive
the_first_city_sunken_archive.description: A lower level beneath the spire, shelved wall to wall with something that isn't quite paper and isn't quite stone. Whoever built this wanted it remembered, not just recorded.

lockables.name: a sealed vault set into the archive's far wall

archive_endless_shelves.name: shelves stretching further back than the light reaches
archive_endless_shelves.description: Every shelf holds the same repeated shape, over and over, for as far as you can see — counting something, still, long after anyone stopped needing the count.

archive_echoing_recess.name: a recess carved deep into the archive's rear wall
archive_echoing_recess.description: Words carved at its edge, worn but legible: "I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind. What am I?"

the_first_city_deepest_record.name: The Deepest Record
the_first_city_deepest_record.description: The lowest chamber anyone's found beneath the spire, walls carved floor to ceiling in the same script found everywhere above — except here, for the first time, it isn't repeating. It's telling something.

the_unrepeating_wall.name: the one wall in the whole buried city that doesn't repeat itself
the_unrepeating_wall.description: Every other surface up above counts the same shape over and over. This one, finally, says something different — though no one still living can read it.

lockables.name: a seam in the floor, hidden beneath old dust

the_first_city_forgotten_depth.name: The Forgotten Depth
the_first_city_forgotten_depth.description: Past the seam in the floor, the carved script gives up its shape completely — the walls here are smooth, black, and warm, like something that stopped bothering to explain itself a long time ago.

whispering_wood_root_hollow.name: The Root Hollow
whispering_wood_root_hollow.description: A hollow beneath the Bramble Thicket's roots, ceiling laced with pale tendrils still faintly warm to the touch. The air smells of turned earth.

resource_nodes.name: a thin seam of ore threading through the roots

hollow_root_lattice.name: the lattice of roots overhead
hollow_root_lattice.description: Every root bends the same direction, all of them curving down and inward, toward wherever the den lies further in.

whispering_wood_sunken_den.name: The Sunken Den
whispering_wood_sunken_den.description: A low, wide den at the end of the roots, floor packed hard by years of restless pacing. Whatever den this is hasn't been abandoned long.

den_claw_marks.name: deep claw marks scored into the packed earth
den_claw_marks.description: Layered thick, over and over, always at the same height — whatever left them never grew any smaller.

whispering_wood_deeper_roots.name: The Deeper Roots
whispering_wood_deeper_roots.description: Past the den, the roots stop looking like roots. They're too regular, too deliberate — less like something that grew here and more like something that was built to look grown.

the_regular_growth.name: a stretch of unnaturally regular root-work
the_regular_growth.description: Every join is the same angle. Whatever grew this whole forest from below, it wasn't growing at random.

greymoor_downs_sunken_barrow.name: The Sunken Barrow
greymoor_downs_sunken_barrow.description: A real camp, still warm in places, dug into the hillside below the Downs — the cold campsite up top was never anything but bait for anyone who stopped looking too soon.

barrow_supply_cache.name: a hidden supply cache dug into the barrow wall
barrow_supply_cache.description: Recently restocked, by the look of it. Whoever uses this place isn't finished with it yet.

stonearch_bridge_gorge_depths.name: The Gorge Depths
stonearch_bridge_gorge_depths.description: The bottom of the gorge beneath the bridge, close and dark, the air moving in and out on a slow rhythm that has nothing to do with wind.

depths_breathing_wall.name: a wide stretch of rock wall, faintly warm
depths_breathing_wall.description: It rises and falls under your palm, slow and even — the same rhythm audible from the bridge far above, only close enough now to feel.

stonearch_bridge_deep_current.name: The Deep Current
stonearch_bridge_deep_current.description: Where the gorge's water finally goes, funneled into a current that runs somewhere no map accounts for. It runs toward the same distant, slow rhythm that fills the depths above.

the_vanishing_current.name: the current itself, vanishing into darker water
the_vanishing_current.description: It never resurfaces anywhere anyone's mapped. Wherever it's actually going, it's going somewhere with purpose.

the_unmoored_isle.name: The Unmoored Isle
the_unmoored_isle.description: An island of grey stone drifting slowly above the clouds, tethered to nothing anyone can see. Something on it has been waiting a very long time.

waiting_shape.name: a still shape at the island's center
waiting_shape.description: Motionless, silhouetted, and unmistakably waiting — for how long, and for what, you can't yet say.

isles_edge.name: the island's crumbling edge
isles_edge.description: Looking over it, the clouds below part just long enough to show how very far down the world actually is.

grimsby.name: Grimsby
grimsby.personality: a gruff but kind-hearted innkeeper who's outlived three generations of regulars and buried more adventurers than he'll admit to
grimsby.goals: wants someone reliable to look into the strange things he won't say out loud

old_maren.name: Old Maren
old_maren.personality: a sharp-tongued trader who has an answer for everything except why she never leaves Market Row after dark

sera_wanderer.name: Sarah
sera_wanderer.personality: a quiet, capable ranger passing through, sizing up anyone who might be worth traveling with
sera_wanderer.goals: looking for a group heading somewhere interesting
activity_goals: scouting the treeline for whatever's been unsettling Grimsby
trading road stories with whoever's willing to listen
helping Old Maren haul in a delivery
sizing up the bridge crossing for safer routes

theron_the_wanderer.name: Theron
theron_the_wanderer.personality: a quiet, unaligned drifter who speaks in riddles and owes loyalty to no one — not unfriendly, but never quite trustworthy either
activity_goals: sitting with the well's warmth, listening for something under it
trading a riddle for a rumor with anyone passing through
walking the tree line without any obvious destination
watching the goblin warrens from a safe distance

kess_the_bandit.name: Kess
kess_the_bandit.personality: a cold, calculating highwaywoman who sizes up travelers as marks before they've even noticed her — cruel by choice, not desperation

ossian_vane.name: Ossian Vane
ossian_vane.personality: a charming, unhurried trader who never quite answers where his stock comes from, and seems to find that question more amusing each time it's asked

borin_ironjaw.name: Borin Ironjaw
borin_ironjaw.personality: a stern, no-nonsense dwarf doing penance for an old failure by watching over the market instead of a castle gate
borin_ironjaw.goals: looking for someone worth vouching for, so he can finally stop watching this street

wren_hollowbrook.name: Wren Hollowbrook
wren_hollowbrook.personality: a quiet half-elf hermit who has tended this shrine's wild garden longer than anyone in town can remember, and speaks more easily to the plants than to people
wren_hollowbrook.goals: protecting the shrine from anyone who'd disturb it without understanding it first

pip_thistledown.name: Pip Thistledown
pip_thistledown.personality: a cheerful halfling bard who's been 'just about to cross' this bridge for three days now, always with one more story first
pip_thistledown.goals: collecting a good enough story to finally justify moving on

grask_emberscale.name: Grask Emberscale
grask_emberscale.personality: a dragonborn barbarian the goblins captured but never quite managed to break, still watching the tunnel entrance for a chance worth taking
grask_emberscale.goals: getting out of these warrens and putting them a long way behind him

vesh_nightglass.name: Vesh Nightglass
vesh_nightglass.personality: a tiefling sorcerer who got turned around chasing a light down here and has been living off crystal-glow for longer than she'll admit
vesh_nightglass.goals: finding someone who actually knows the way back to the surface

marens_wares.description: Old Maren's stall sprawls across three tables — a weapon rack, a rack of hung armor, and shelves of tools and provisions, every price scratched straight into the wood in her own tally-marks.

vanes_curiosities.description: Ossian Vane's corner of the Arcane Nook — scrolls pinned in neat rows, a locked case of stranger things, and a ledger he never quite lets anyone read.

grimsbys_tavern.description: Grimsby keeps a short shelf behind the bar — ale, rations, and just enough healing to get a rough night behind you.

welcome_to_the_crossroads.title: A Favor for Grimsby
welcome_to_the_crossroads.description: Grimsby has noticed something's off in the Whispering Wood and wants eyes on it.
welcome_to_the_crossroads.clue: Grimsby says the wrongness he's felt seems to trail off toward the treeline west of the tavern.

seras_safer_crossing.title: Sarah's Safer Crossing
seras_safer_crossing.description: Sarah's been sizing up the Stonearch Bridge crossing, uneasy about who else might be using it to move unseen -- she'd rather have a second set of eyes before trusting the route.
seras_safer_crossing.clue: Sarah says she'll feel better about the bridge once someone's actually walked it with her.

seras_resolution.title: Worth Traveling With
seras_resolution.description: Sarah's spent long enough sizing up this party to have an answer now, one way or another -- she wants to give it to you back at the bridge crossing where she first asked for a second set of eyes.
seras_resolution.clue: Sarah keeps glancing down the far road out of town, like she's still weighing whether to take it.

borins_vouching_task.title: A Name Worth Vouching For
borins_vouching_task.description: Borin's done penance on this street long enough to know he can't vouch for anyone he hasn't actually seen handle real danger -- he wants the party to deal with whatever's really going on in the Goblin Warrens before he'll put his name behind them.
borins_vouching_task.clue: Borin says a name means nothing until it's been tested somewhere that actually matters.

borins_resolution.title: The Watch He Keeps
borins_resolution.description: Borin's tested the party in the Warrens like he said he would -- now it's just a matter of whether he actually believes his own penance is paid, standing right back where he's stood watch this whole time.
borins_resolution.clue: Borin still takes up the same spot on Market Row every morning, like he hasn't decided anything yet.

wrens_root_worry.title: What the Roots Are Hiding
wrens_root_worry.description: Wren's shrine draws on something growing down in the Sunken Root Caverns, and lately it's felt wrong -- she wants someone who isn't afraid of the dark to go see what's changed down there.
wrens_root_worry.clue: Wren says the shrine's garden has been restless the same way it was the last time something changed down below.

wrens_resolution.title: Roots Worth Trusting
wrens_resolution.description: Wren's let the party into the Sunken Root Caverns once already -- now it's a matter of whether she'll actually tell them what the shrine's roots are drawing on, back where she's kept that secret all along.
wrens_resolution.clue: Wren keeps almost saying something about the shrine's roots, then talking to the garden instead.

pips_story_worth_telling.title: A Story Worth Telling
pips_story_worth_telling.description: Pip's been stalling on this bridge for three days waiting for one good story before he'll finally move on -- he wants the party to bring back proof of something genuinely worth singing about from the Whispering Wood.
pips_story_worth_telling.clue: Pip says a story only counts if he can honestly say he sent someone to go get it.

pips_resolution.title: The Story He's Already In
pips_resolution.description: Pip got his story out of the Whispering Wood -- now it's just a matter of whether he realizes the better one's been happening around him this whole time, back on the same bridge he's been stalling on for days.
pips_resolution.clue: Pip's still saying he's 'just about to cross,' but he's stopped actually packing to leave.

grasks_freedom.title: Grask's Freedom
grasks_freedom.description: Grask has been watching the tunnel entrance for a chance worth taking ever since the goblins caught him -- the party dealing with what's really running this warren is exactly the chance he's been waiting for.
grasks_freedom.clue: Grask says whoever's giving these goblins their orders is the only thing standing between him and the surface.

grasks_resolution.title: Grask's Choice
grasks_resolution.description: Every step back down has been against everything Grask swore to himself once he got out -- and he's taking every one of them anyway, because the party asked, not because the warrens ever let go of him.
grasks_resolution.clue: Grask keeps saying he's done with tunnels, then keeps following the party into the next one.

veshs_way_back.title: Vesh's Way Back
veshs_way_back.description: Vesh got turned around chasing a light down into Glimmerdeep Grotto and has been living off crystal-glow ever since -- she just wants someone who actually knows the way to walk her back up to The Crossroads Tavern.
veshs_way_back.clue: Vesh says she stopped trying to count the days once the crystal-glow started tasting normal.

veshs_resolution.title: Back Down Into the Glow
veshs_resolution.description: The party needs someone who's actually been past Glimmerdeep Grotto before, and Vesh is the only one who has -- which means going back to exactly the place she spent this long trying to forget.
veshs_resolution.clue: Vesh goes quiet every time the crystal-glow comes up again.

the_hollow_stump.title: The Hollow Stump
the_hollow_stump.description: The shrine in the Whispering Wood may hold answers to what's been left behind there.
the_hollow_stump.clue: Old offerings at the shrine are undisturbed by animals — worth seeing with your own eyes.

clear_the_warrens.title: Clear the Goblin Warrens
clear_the_warrens.description: The goblins under Stonearch Bridge have grown bold. Someone should find out why.
clear_the_warrens.clue: Whatever's emboldened the goblins seems to answer to something bigger among them.

the_wrong_color.title: The Wrong Color
the_wrong_color.description: Something in Glimmerdeep Grotto is changing the crystals. Investigate.
the_wrong_color.clue: Travelers who've passed the Sunken Root Caverns mention a faint, wrong-colored light deeper in.

the_hush_stage1_signs.title: Into the Hush
the_hush_stage1_signs.description: No two accounts of what's past Glimmerdeep Grotto agree — that alone is worth noting. The only way to know for certain is to go down and see it yourself.
the_hush_stage1_signs.clue: No two accounts of what's past Glimmerdeep Grotto agree — that alone is worth noting.

the_hush_stage2_the_wisp.title: What Watches in the Dark
the_hush_stage2_the_wisp.description: Something pale and quick moves at the edge of every torch's reach down here, blinding anyone who gets too close a good look at it — it has to be dealt with before whatever's deeper even notices you've arrived.
the_hush_stage2_the_wisp.clue: Footprints in old dust, fresh enough that the dust hasn't resettled — something else is already down here.

the_hush_stage3_the_unspoken.title: What Answers Back
the_hush_stage3_the_unspoken.description: Few who go into the Hush Below come back describing the same thing twice — and something down there has started describing YOU back, in a voice that isn't quite a voice.
the_hush_stage3_the_unspoken.clue: An old iron door, ajar, wasn't open a moment ago — whatever moved it wants to be found now.

the_first_city_quest.title: The First City
the_first_city_quest.description: Beneath everything, something predates the goblins, the roots, and the crystals — and the spire's slow, warm breathing has just changed rhythm.
the_first_city_quest.clue: Everything so far has felt like the edge of something older, further down.

the_unmoored_isle_quest.title: What Waits Above
the_unmoored_isle_quest.description: The sky itself is not as empty as it looks — something has been waiting at the island's center for a very long time, and it's noticed you.
the_unmoored_isle_quest.clue: The shard you carry seems to want to go up, not down.

marens_locked_ledger.title: Maren's Locked Ledger
marens_locked_ledger.description: Old Maren has an old strongbox she's lost the combination to, and swears there's a riddle carved into its lid that used to be the answer.
marens_locked_ledger.clue: The riddle carved into the lid reads: "I have cities, but no houses; forests, but no trees; rivers, but no water. What am I?"

the_elder_glens_riddle.title: The Elder Glen's Riddle
the_elder_glens_riddle.description: Words carved into the widest tree in the Elder Glen — old enough that whoever carved them is long gone, but the question still stands.
the_elder_glens_riddle.clue: The words carved into the tree read: "I have many rings but no fingers, many arms but no hands, and I tell your age without ever asking. What am I?"

the_archives_recess.title: The Archive's Recess
the_archives_recess.description: A recess carved into the rear wall of the Sunken Archive, words worn into its edge — whoever carved them wanted this one specifically remembered.
the_archives_recess.clue: The words carved at the recess's edge read: "I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind. What am I?"

the_weeping_wells_secret.title: The Weeping Well's Secret
the_weeping_wells_secret.description: Sarah thinks the well's strange warmth isn't natural, and that whatever's behind it is worth finding, not just noting.
the_weeping_wells_secret.clue: Sarah says the sealed door low in the well's wall is the only part of it that isn't carved from ordinary stone.

the_unrepeating_depth.title: What Finally Speaks
the_unrepeating_depth.description: Past the seam in the Deepest Record's floor, the walls stop repeating themselves entirely — and whatever kept them company down here is done waiting to be read.
the_unrepeating_depth.clue: Nothing about this place was ever part of the story everyone else was told.

arc_1_discovery.title: Discovery
arc_1_discovery.description: Small, strange things, easy to explain away individually.

arc_2_descent.title: The Descent
arc_2_descent.description: The pattern beneath the strangeness starts to surface.

arc_3_revelation.title: What Was Buried
arc_3_revelation.description: The truth of what the surface world was built on top of.

arc_4_ascension.title: What Waits Above
arc_4_ascension.description: The final confrontation, far from where anyone thought to look.

crossroads_folk.name: The Crossroads Folk
crossroads_folk.description: The ordinary people who keep the Crossroads running — innkeepers, traders, and the wanderers who pass through and stay a while. No oaths, no hierarchy, just people who look out for each other.

blackthorn_raiders.name: The Blackthorn Raiders
blackthorn_raiders.description: A loose band of highwaymen and opportunists preying on the roads between settlements. Small, cruel, and — some in the Crossroads whisper — funded by something bigger than banditry.

the_wanderers_road.name: The Wanderers' Road
the_wanderers_road.description: An informal fellowship of drifters, hermits, and those who owe allegiance to no settlement or crown. Neither friend nor enemy by default — standing with them is earned entirely by what you actually do.

marens_riddle.riddle: I have cities, but no houses; forests, but no trees; rivers, but no water. What am I?

elder_glen_riddle.riddle: I have many rings but no fingers, many arms but no hands, and I tell your age without ever asking. What am I?

archive_recess_riddle.riddle: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body, but I come alive with wind. What am I?
